orbits.name: Space Station orbit
orbits.tooltip: Low and easy to reach, but the thin air up there slowly drags the craft down. It never passes over the far north or south.
orbits.sourceNote: CubeSat 101 section 3.5: CubeSats released from the Space Station share its orbit. Revisit is a rounded estimate.

orbits.name: Sun-synchronous orbit
orbits.tooltip: Goes over the poles and passes each place at the same time of day, so every photo has the same lighting. A favourite for Earth-watching satellites.
orbits.sourceNote: Typical Earth-observation orbit. Revisit and sun angle are rounded estimates.

orbits.name: Geostationary orbit (GEO)
orbits.tooltip: So high that one orbit takes a whole day, so the craft seems to hover over one spot. Great for watching weather, but very far away and hard to reach.
orbits.sourceNote: 35,786 km is the altitude where one orbit takes one day.

decaySource.sourceNote: Rounded typical lifetimes for a small craft with average solar activity. To check against GMAT runs; real decay changes a lot with the solar cycle.

disposalSource.sourceNote: CubeSat 101 section 6.1: an orbital debris report must show the craft will deorbit in a reasonable time. We use NASA's 25-year guideline; FCC-licensed craft now face a stricter 5-year rule.
